sentences.text: As per prosecution case in brief, informant , who is father of the victim, has lodged an FIR on 22.03.2022 with regard to an incident which took place on 21.03.2022 against the applicant for the alleged offence under Section 354(A) IPC and Sections 7/8 of POCSO Act alleging inter alia that his daughter, aged about nine years, was playing outside her house and when he went to call her, he came to know that the Munna took his daughter to forest.
While searching his daughter in the forest, he saw that Munna was molesting his daughter by touching her delicate parts.

It is contended by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant has been languishing in jail since 11.04.2022 but till date, trial of the applicant has not been concluded, therefore, considering the detention period of the applicant, he is entitled to be released on bail.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State vehemently opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that the victim is a minor girl aged about 12 years and she in her examination-in-chief recorded before the trial Court on 01.03.2023 has made serious allegation of rape against the applicant giving vivid description of the incident.
Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perusing the statement of the minor victim recorded before the trial Court, I do not find any good ground to enlarge the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the instant second bail application is rejected.
It is made clear that the observation contained in the instant order is confined to the issue of bail and shall not affect the merit of the trial.

However, the trial Court is directed to make an endeavour to conclude the trial expeditiously without granting any unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties from the date of production of a copy of this order.
